gaps.sentence: We should make the ___ of the good weather.
gaps.explanation: 'make the most of' = get the maximum benefit from.

gaps.sentence: The film is based ___ a true story.
The meeting has been ___ forward to Monday.
gaps.explanation: 'bring forward' = move to an earlier time (opposite of put off).

gaps.sentence: She made the cake ___, without any help at all.
gaps.explanation: 'She made it herself' — the reflexive stresses she did it alone.

gaps.sentence: She's very good ___ explaining difficult ideas.
All the tickets ___ sold out by noon.
gaps.explanation: Past perfect passive: had been + participle (before the stated past moment).

gaps.sentence: It was ___ a lovely evening that nobody wanted to leave.
gaps.explanation: 'Such a lovely evening that …' — 'so' would go directly before an adjective.

gaps.sentence: I'd like to know when the results ___ be published.
gaps.explanation: Future in a noun clause: when the results will be published.
